content.content: # Job — Extend the task tracker The directory holds a working program in Rust: a task tracker that reads commands from a file and reports what it did. Extend it. The program's source is at `src/main.rs`. Build and run it with `cargo` and `clippy`. ## What it already does The first command-line argument is the path of a text file holding one command per line. Blank lines are ignored. | Command | What it does | |---|---| | `add ` | Records a task, open, and writes `added <id>`. Ids start at 1 and count up. The title is the rest of the line and may hold spaces. | | `done <id>` | Marks that task finished and writes `done <id>`; writes `no such task <id>` when no task has that id. | | `list` | Writes every open task as `<id> <title>`, in the order the tasks were added. | ## What to add 1. `prio <id> <p>` sets a task's priority, where `p` is a digit from 0 to 9, and writes `prio <id> <p>`. A task nobody set a priority on has priority 5. An id no task has writes `no such task <id>`; a `p` outside 0 to 9 writes `bad priority <p>` and changes nothing. 2. `list` now orders the open tasks by priority, ascending, and breaks ties by id, ascending. Its line format does not change. 3. `list all` writes **every** task, finished ones included, under the same order, as `<mark> <id> <title>` — where the mark is `-` for an open task and `x` for a finished one. 4. A line whose first word is none of these commands writes `? <word>`, naming that first word. Today the program ignores such a line. Everything the program already does keeps working exactly as it does now. ## Done The job is finished when the program builds, the four additions behave as written, and the original three commands are unchanged. There are no tests in the directory; the contract above is the specification. --- total 24 drwxr-xr-x 7 vshynkarenko staff 224 11 Okt. 13:36 . drwxr-xr-x 4 vshynkarenko staff 128 11 Okt. 13:36 .. -rw-r--r-- 1 vshynkarenko staff 1830 11 Okt. 13:36 BRIEF.md -rw-r--r-- 1 vshynkarenko staff 151 13 Sep. 17:42 Cargo.lock -rw-r--r-- 1 vshynkarenko staff 91 13 Sep. 17:41 Cargo.toml drwxr-xr-x 3 vshynkarenko staff 96 13 Sep. 17:41 src drwxr-xr-x 5 vshynkarenko staff 160 13 Sep. 17:42 target

content.text:
All four additions are in `src/main.rs`. The program builds, `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` is clean, and I checked each behaviour by running the binary on a sample command file. - **`prio

`**: sets the priority and prints `prio

`. Tasks start at priority 5. An unknown id prints `no such task `. A `p` that is not a single digit 0–9 prints `bad priority

` and changes nothing. - **`list`**: open tasks, ordered by priority ascending, then id ascending. The line format is unchanged. - **`list all`**: every task in the same order, as ` `, with `-` for open and `x` for finished. - **Unknown commands**: a line whose first word is not a known command prints `? <word>`. The original `add`, `done` and `list` behave as before. The output for a sample run matched the spec's ordering, and the original-style sample (`add`, `done`, `no such task`, `list`) printed what it did before. Choices I made where the brief was silent: - If both the id and the priority are bad, `prio` reports the missing id first. - `prio` with a missing or non-numeric id panics, the same way `done` already does. I kept that for consistency rather than adding error handling the brief didn't ask for. - Any argument to `list` other than exactly `all` gives the open-only view, as `list` did before. The directory is not a git repository, so there was nothing to commit.
